openQuestions.question: Is the wait for the next service the exact timetable wait from the player's arrival, or an average of half the headway?
openQuestions.why: The GDD says price = wait + ride from the timetable but does not say how the wait is computed.

openQuestions.question: What walking pace and route apply to an interchange between stops?
openQuestions.why: The GDD states no walking pace. 1.4 m/s is used as an [S] placeholder.

openQuestions.question: Can a player board a service already dwelling at the stop, and does dwell count as wait?
openQuestions.why: The GDD does not decide this, and it affects the cost of a tight interchange.

openQuestions.question: Should boarding ever carry a cost beyond time (a fare)?
openQuestions.why: GDD §02 says time only, no fare. Nothing is assumed here; raised only in case a design change is wanted.

notes: T1 and T2 speed 8 m/s [S]: stops are 300–500 m apart (tram standard), so runs of about 38–58 s are readable and trams stay slower than the sky rail. Dwell 15 s, headway 120 s. T2 added with the same values as T1 so every candidate line has a timetable.
S1 speed 12 m/s [S]: stations are 200–500 m apart and the beam is 24 m up, so runs of about 17–21 s keep the sky rail the quicker network. Dwell 12 s, headway 90 s.
Headways, dwells and speeds are all [S] starting values, to be tuned by playtest.
Boarding is priced in time only: the wait for the next service (from headway) plus the ride. No fare (GDD §02 travel). The earlier fare note is removed.
Interchange pairs used: T1/circus with S1/circus, T1/comet with T2/comet, S1/harbour with T2/parade. The Crown Circus pair is about 119 m apart by candidate coordinates, inside the 150 m limit.

Mismatch: the plan passage gives S1 Crown Circus at 95 and Harbour at 340, while the candidate lines and stop table use 90 and 290. I used the stop table and left both unchanged. Datum should confirm which is current.

handoffs.ask: Confirm S1 station chainage: plan text says Crown Circus 95 and Harbour 340; the stop table uses 90 and 290.
